power net V3_3 runs at 0.2mm — the same copper as a signal. The current maths may pass on this board, but power at signal width is the wrong habit; the profile's power floor is 0.5mm (warn_power_trace_mm — an EE moves the line there)

net USB_DM reaches only U3 — every pin on it belongs to the same part, so whatever was meant to be on the other end of this net is not on the board. The copper that exists is correct, which is why nothing else reports it; the wire that does not exist is the defect. Either connect it, or name it TP*/NC* to say the pad is the point

net USB_DP reaches only U3 — every pin on it belongs to the same part, so whatever was meant to be on the other end of this net is not on the board. The copper that exists is correct, which is why nothing else reports it; the wire that does not exist is the defect. Either connect it, or name it TP*/NC* to say the pad is the point

U2's nearest decoupling capacitor to pin VIN is 9.7mm away; the loop inductance is what does the work, so keep it inside 5mm (1 pin(s) are further)
U3's nearest decoupling capacitor to pin IOVDD3 is 6.1mm away; the loop inductance is what does the work, so keep it inside 5mm (2 pin(s) are further)
2 pin(s) of U3 are alone on their net and connect to nothing (USB_DM, USB_DP). An input left floating picks up whatever is nearby; a strap pin left floating boots at random
1 rail(s) have nowhere to put a probe (V3_3). Add a test point — nobody can diagnose a dead board over chat without one
U2 dissipates 0.23W at 134mA and sits about 59 degC junction, 66 degC inside the limit
